interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is reported absent. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 32.32 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 25.86–38.79 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Preoperative PSA was elevated at 5.8. The surgical findings included a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), pT2 stage with no extraprostatic extension, positive surgical margins, and invasion of the seminal vesicles was absent. A key finding is the presence of lymph node metastasis. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing from the biopsy. The nodal status is documented as positive lymph node metastasis.

Countervailing factors include the absence of lymphovascular invasion and the absence of extraprostatic extension. Missing nodal sampling information would widen the uncertainty regarding nodal status. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are critical unknowns that would significantly revise this prognosis. The current heuristic horizon suggests a follow-up period of approximately 32 months without an event.

nodal_contradiction: Missing nodal sampling information would widen the uncertainty regarding nodal status

attempts.text:
The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage pT2, Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), positive surgical margins, and the seminal vesicles were not invaded. Lymph node metastasis was present. Preoperative PSA was 5.8. The surgical findings include positive margins and documented lymph node metastasis, which are factors driving the prognosis toward increased risk. The absence of extraprostatic extension and seminal vesicle invasion are favorable findings.

The preoperative PSA level and the presence of lymph node metastasis are key documented factors influencing the outcome. The positive surgical margins and nodal involvement represent adverse findings. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing. Missing nodal sampling information would widen the uncertainty regarding nodal status. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are critical pieces of information that would revise the prognosis. The current heuristic horizon for recurrence is 32.3 months.
